exposure.name: REGISTRANT_SUBJECT_TO_A_LEGAL_MATTER
exposure.why: The registrant (or a party it names) is subject to, involved in, party to or a defendant in a legal matter.

exposure.name: REGISTRANT_IS_A_PARTY
exposure.why: A matter 'in which it was a plaintiff'; 'matters in which we are a defendant'.

exposure.name: ACCRUAL
exposure.why: An accrual the registrant makes; the adjudicated rule CLAIMS_ACCRUAL_IS_DISCLOSURE (self-insured claims, a litigation accrual review).

exposure.name: RECORDED_LIABILITY_CHARGE_OR_BENEFIT
exposure.why: An amount the registrant records: a benefit from stockholder litigation, a liability for claims.

exposure.name: SELF_INSURED
exposure.why: Self-insurance for the registrant's own claims.

exposure.name: A_MATTER_IN_A_COURT
exposure.why: The vocabulary of a specific proceeding: a filing, a court, an allegation, a ruling, a party. 'judgments' alone is not here: an accounting estimate is 'based on complex judgments'.

exposure.name: SETTLEMENT_OF_A_LEGAL_MATTER
exposure.why: A settlement of a legal matter. Settlements with taxing authorities are not one (a tax-position paragraph).

exposure.name: REGISTRANT_EXPOSED_TO_OR_NAMED_IN_A_LEGAL_MATTER
exposure.why: The same relation as being subject to a legal matter, worded as exposure or as being named in one.

exposure.name: A_MATTER_AGAINST_THE_REGISTRANT
exposure.why: A matter directed at the registrant ('claims against the Company', 'brought against us').

exposure.name: A_MATTER_BROUGHT_BY_OR_AGAINST_A_PARTY
exposure.why: A matter someone brought or asserted: a category is not brought by anyone.

exposure.name: A_SUIT_OR_AN_ARBITRATION
exposure.why: Suing, being sued, or an arbitration: the vocabulary of a particular matter, like 'filed' or 'court'.

exposure.name: REGISTRANT_FACES_A_LEGAL_MATTER
exposure.why: Facing a legal matter is the relation of being subject to one, worded with the verb: 'our company faced litigation, regulatory proceedings and fines' (#28's review of its copy of version 2).

why_this_file: Version 4 of the D02 Item 8 category-mention terms. Version 3 read a coordinated series as a category unless the registrant was named before it; a series with no closed-class word governing it still left - 'Kestrel defended regulatory proceedings, litigation and fines.' (the registrant by its own name, an open-class verb) and 'In 2025, litigation, fines and penalties increased.' (the series as subject) - which #28 reproduced on its copy (Issue #47 comment 5956052190). Version 4 keeps every pattern of version 3 unchanged; its reader now removes a list member only when a closed-class governor is proven for the series (a preposition, 'including' or 'such as' before its first member, not opening the sentence), as version 3 already required where the registrant was named. Every pattern here is closed-class grammar or the vocabulary of a legal matter; business phrases live here rather than in executable code (tools/check_vnext_semantics.py); the file's bytes are recorded by the issue_47_v1 snapshot as a rule file, so a change here moves the Requirement closure.
